futureAppearances.label: Exam 3 — probing index from raw hash
futureAppearances.description: Problem 4(a)/(b) ask for the first four indices a hash value visits under quadratic and linear probing. The mod-by-capacity step is the same arithmetic that maps stringHashCode output to a bucket in your separate-chaining table.

concepts.concept: Separate chaining: collision resolution by adding to the front of a bucket's list

futureAppearances.label: Exam 3 — separate chaining T/F
futureAppearances.description: Problem 1(c) ('every entry of the chained array stores either a node-reference or null') tests the same invariant your toRawString output displays — bucket = head-of-chain or null.

futureAppearances.label: Exam 3 — numCollidedEntries (practice)
futureAppearances.description: The practice exam asks you to count entries that hashed into a non-empty bucket. The same per-bucket walk you do in toRawString is what lets you decide whether a particular add 'collided'.

futureAppearances.label: Exam 3 — minimum adds to trigger first rehash
futureAppearances.description: Problem 4(c)(ii) asks how many adds are needed before the table grows. With M=10 and λ ≤ .60 the answer is 7 — same lambda-threshold arithmetic you implemented for HW7 with M=5 and λ ≤ 2.

futureAppearances.label: Exam 3 — rehash diagram
futureAppearances.description: Problem 4(c)(iii) requires re-bucketing five items into a doubled-capacity chained table — the same redistribution your testAddAndRawStringRehash exercises after the 11th add.

futureAppearances.label: Final Exam — issues in hash table implementation
futureAppearances.description: The Final's hash content is conceptual: capacity choice, load-factor selection, and amortized-vs-worst-case cost of rehash all show up as discussion questions you can answer from your own implementation experience.
